title: Lookahead Econ Sandbox Intro - Sparrow Ventures
summary: Intro to Redwood Optimize sandbox focused on lookahead/prefetch economics, walk through batch sizing, session affinity, and a cost model demo. Customer is interested in hosted vs private tradeoffs for low-latency chat, wants a sandbox to run 2-week cost/latency sims and a security review. Agreed pilot scope and next steps.

batch sizing and throughput vs p95 latency tradeoffs
KV/prefix caching economics and hit lifecycle
sandbox cost model walkthrough (token / GPU cost mapping)

SE to run baseline cost sim with current prompt set and share CSV + spreadsheet by 2026-11-20

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-17 16:00 PT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marcus (Redwood Solutions), Aisha (Sparrow Head of ML), Tom (Sparrow Cloud Eng), Leila (Sparrow Product)

Auto-summary (auto): quick demo of Optimize sandbox, Q&A on caching, then next steps on security + pilot

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros?
[00:06] Aisha: Hi, I'm Aisha, head of ML at Sparrow. we're trying to reduce token cost for our chat assistant while keeping p95 under 250 ms end-to-end.
[00:15] Tom: Tom here, I manage infra and networking. we'll need VPC constraints, also KMS for keys.
[00:19] Leila: Leila, product, I'll own success criteria for the pilot.
[00:24] Jordan: Awesome. Priya, Marcus, quick opener?
[00:27] Priya: Hi all, SE Priya. today we'll show lookahead/prefetch in Optimize, run a quick cost sim and show how batching + KV/prefix caching interact.
[00:36] Marcus: And I'll demo the sandbox UI, the heatmaps and sim controls.

[03:05] Priya: First high-level: lookahead or 'prefetch' means we materialize likely next-token KV state for warm sessions so subsequent requests hit cache and avoid full decode. big win for multi-turn chat where users have short follow-ups.
[03:32] Aisha: right, we have lots of short turn exchanges, 60% are < 20 tokens followups. so this seems relevant.

[06:10] Marcus: here's the sandbox UI — showing traffic histogram, session affinity options, and prefetch policy toggles. (link: sandbox playbook)
[06:30] [Speaker 2]: note, transcription may flip some product names, e.g., 'Optimize' got heard as 'opt-in'.

[08:12] Priya: Ok demo scenario one: baseline hosted inference with no prefetch, batch size 8, sequence length average 256, concurrency 24. p95 we measured at 280 ms on these kernels, token cost $0.0006/token (example, simplified).
[08:38] Tom: can you map that cost to our monthly? our batched traffic is about 8 million tokens/day.
[08:45] Priya: quick calc: 8M * 30 = 240M tokens/month * 0.0006 = ~ $144k/month raw token cost, ignoring infra and reserved discounts. the sandbox sim will give more granular GPU-hours mapping.

[11:02] Priya: Scenario two: enable lookahead / prefix KV for sessionized flows. hit rate assumptions matter — we set a conservative 35% hit rate for warm prefetch. that reduced token decode by ~18% in our sim and improved p95 by about 40 ms due to shorter decode paths.
[11:30] Aisha: how sensitive is that to cold start of sessions or user variability?
[11:35] Priya: good q. the hit lifecycle matters — TTLs, eviction windows, and session affinity all change effective hit rate. we show a hit-life histogram in the sandbox so you can tune TTL to your user pattern.

[14:20] Marcus: switching to batch sizing: we ran three configs: small batch (4), medium (12), large (32). throughput scales up as expected but p95 climbs with large batches under low concurrency. Optimize can automatically pick batch size per latency policy or you can pin.
[14:50] Tom: for us, p95 target is 250 ms; which tradeoff would you pick?
[14:55] Priya: with your traffic shape (many short followups), I'd recommend medium batching + lookahead. That gives decent throughput and keeps p95 around 230–260 depending on sequence tails. sandbox will give exact numbers with your trace.

[18:05] Leila: curious about dedicated vs hosted — we need strict data isolation for some customers and possibly on-prem later. what's the difference for caching?
[18:18] Jordan: hosted Optimize can do most prefetch and cache optimizations. Dedicated or Private gives you the same runtime but with isolated pools and the private control plane. KV encryption and KMS integration are supported on Private. There is some additional setup time for Private and reserved capacity costs.
[18:46] Tom: do we need extra networking for KV lookahead in VPC?
[18:50] Marcus: normally KV shard lives co-located with model runtime; in VPC we use internal endpoints. no external egress. we'll run a short network checklist in the VPC deep dive.

[22:30] Priya: walk through cost model spreadsheet: columns are scenario, tokens avoided, GPU-hours saved, estimated $ savings, and risk notes. I uploaded the sample to the sandbox sheet. link: https://redwood.ai/sandbox/ff-88491/cost-model.csv
[22:50] Aisha: are you modeling quantization/low-bit variants? some of our models are q4_0 and q8_0 variants.
[22:58] Priya: yes we include quantization tiers. lower precision reduces decode cost but can slightly impact generation quality. in the sim we show quality deltas per prompt set so you can verify.

[26:12] Jordan: there's often confusion around 'session cache' vs 'lookahead'. session cache is storing full prefix KV for ongoing sessions; lookahead precomputes likely next KVs for a short window — both help but have different storage/compute profiles.
[26:37] Tom: storage cost for prefix cache?
[26:41] Priya: depends on average prefix length and saved KVs per session. rough rule: 1M active sessions with average prefix 3MB of KV => ~3TB which has cost and eviction policy implications. we'll surface exact estimates in the sandbox.

[30:01] Aisha: security: we need SOC2 type II, SSO integration, and KMS. anything else?
[30:08] Jordan: we have SOC2 and ISO docs; SAML SSO supported, SCIM for provisioning, KMS for key rotation. we'll share the security pack after the call.
[30:20] Leila: also audit logs per token/session?
[30:23] Marcus: yes, Console has per-request tracing and event logs; retention configurable as an add-on.

[33:50] Priya: demo of heatmap and TTL tuning — increasing TTL increases hit rate but also memory usage and staleness risk. we toggled TTL from 30s to 2 minutes and saw hit rate go from 28% to 46% for this trace, with incremental CPU cost for prefetching at the start of sessions.
[34:20] Aisha: interesting, 46% would be a big win. what's the downside?
[34:24] Priya: stale context for long-lived sessions if you prefetch aggressively, and extra prefetch compute which inflates short-term GPU usage. sandbox sim will show these tradeoffs per your session length distribution.

[37:10] Tom: network egress and data residency — if we run in EU region, does the sandbox reflect region pricing?
[37:15] Marcus: yes; sandbox can simulate region-specific kerner costs and GPU pricing. we can spin infra in eu-west for your tests.

[40:05] Jordan: quick objection handling: customers often worry about unpredictability of caching. best practice is conservative TTLs and gradual canary rollouts. we offer canary rollout controls in Console.
[40:22] Aisha: and monitoring? we need alerting when hit rates or latency regress.
[40:28] Marcus: Console has dashboards, alerting rules and export hooks to your pagerduty. we'll configure a few recommended alerts in the sandbox.

[44:00] (Side discussion: pricing nuance)
[44:12] Priya: note that reserved Dedicated capacity gives predictable per-GPU cost and is often cheaper at scale than hosted on-demand token pricing — but it does require a commit. For a 3-6 month pilot, hosted sandbox is easiest to iterate.
[44:35] Tom: we likely want hosted sandbox first then evaluate Dedicated if the economics work out.

[47:50] Jordan: recap and concrete next steps — we'll provision sandbox, SE will run baseline and three batch/prefetch sims, you'll provide prompt sets and trace, and we'll do a security packet share.
[48:10] Leila: can we get a short 30-min follow-up specifically on VPC networking?
[48:14] Jordan: yes, we'll schedule that for week of 11/23.

[52:05] Aisha: one last thing — our product wants an ROI number to show leadership. can you produce a 3-scenario ROI (conservative, expected, optimistic)?
[52:13] Priya: yes, that's part of the cost-model deliverable. we'll include an ROI table and explain assumptions.

[55:00] Jordan: thanks all. we'll email the sandbox invite and security docs today.
[55:07] Tom: thanks, bye.
[55:09] Leila: thanks everyone.
[55:10] Marcus: thanks, bye.

End of transcript.

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-attributions and abbreviated technical terms consistent with automated transcription. Shared artifacts: Optimize sandbox link (https://app.redwood.ai/sandbox/ff-88491), cost-model CSV (https://redwood.ai/sandbox/ff-88491/cost-model.csv), security pack placeholder (to be emailed).
questions: How sensitive are prefetch hit rates to session TTL and user variance?
What is the estimated storage footprint for prefix cache at Sparrow's scale?
Can we run the sandbox in eu-west for region-specific pricing and latency sim?
